title: Confirmations (M11)
brief: Confirm pattern for hard-to-undo actions, restyled to share the command palette's box, tiles and rows. A centered ~600px box on --background-panel with a 1px --text-muted border on all four sides (no radius, no shadow, no colored edge, no esc label) sits over the dimmed, inert 04 session. Main frame: Delete all goop data? (from Privacy M13). Header: an --error tile with a trash glyph in --background, the question as a bold label and the muted subline From Privacy · everything goop stored on this machine. Palette-style rows with tile, label and a muted right-aligned count under small uppercase labels: Deleted (Offers 412 --success, Sessions 7 --text-muted, Rules 7 --accent, Profile and CV cv-2026.pdf --accent, Encrypted database 38 MB --text-muted) and Stays, dimmed (Downloaded models 31 GB · reusable, --primary). A bold --error line This cannot be undone. goop keeps no backup. The type-to-confirm input is the palette search line at the bottom of the box under a --border-subtle separator: dele typed, lavender cursor, muted type delete to confirm on the right. No hint row inside: the status line shows confirm (--error dot), type delete · ↵ delete (muted until it matches) · esc cancel (green safe default), ○ next 09:00 │ ? help. Strip below: (1) reversible inline one-line ask Dismiss 3 offers? y yes · n no plus the undo toast; (2) costly Unfollow 3 companies? as a small bordered box with an --accent tile, Acme Labs, Kraft and Orbit rows with --secondary tiles, the muted line They stop being searched. Their offers stay in your list. and y unfollow · n keep; (3) the matched confirm line delete · matches with a note that ↵ now deletes. Notes with the three-level table.

artboards.title: Dialog levels
artboards.tradeoff: One box style for every modal, so the confirm reads as part of the palette family and the tiles show by color what the loss touches, while a stray enter can never delete; but the bordered box stops being palette-only, the danger rests on one pink tile and the warning line instead of a pink edge (quieter), the confirm word is English in a Spanish chat, and each new action needs its level chosen at design time
